3. The Assistant Judge and House Rent Controller, Rangpur in Miscellaneous Case No. 90 of 1990 dismissed the case of the plaintiff-respondent under section 19(1) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, 1963. On appeal by the plaintiff-respondent, the learned Subordinate Judge, Rangpur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 7 of 1992 affirmed the judgment passed by the Senior Assistant Judge and dismissed the appeal. The appellate Court found that as per contract and also as per section 18 of the Ordinance the petitioner failed to pay the rent within 15 days of the subsequent month, as such, he dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and order of the Assistant Judge. 

 4. The plaintiff-respondent then took the matter to the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3552 of 1995. The High Court Division found that the plaintiff-respondent had sent the rent for the month of January to June, 1990 in lump by postal money order. The same was returned back on 5-6-90 and the plaintiff-respondent. Therefore deposited the same by filing the aforementioned Miscellaneous Case No. 90 of 1990 before the Assistant Judge on 18-6-90. This fact has escaped consideration of the courts below. The courts below, considered the evidence of PW 1 who in cross examination stated that the respondent had deposited the rent within 15 days from the date of return of the money order, but this oral evidence was not proved and documentary evidence showed that the money order was returned on 5-6-90 and the respondent deposited the, rent by filing miscellaneous case on 18-6-90 with the House Rent Controller. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division then considered the provisions of section 19(1)(Ka) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance 1963 which reads as follows: 

 As the rent was sent back to the plaintiff- respondent on 5-6-90 which was sent by postal money order he deposited the same with House Rent Controller by filing aforementioned miscellaneous case on 18-6-90  ie well within time to deposit the rent with the House Rent Controller as per above provisions. As such the High Court Division held that the decision of the courts below could not be sustainable in law and therefore, made the Rule absolute. We find that the courts below overlooked the fact that the rent deposited under the miscellaneous case was within the time as laid down in section 19(Ka) ie within 15 days of refusal and the High Court Division correctly noticed that this fact escaped consideration of the courts below. It appears that the trial Court and the appellate Court wrongly decided the case holding that the plaintiff-respondent had failed to pay rent within 15 days of subsequent month as per section 18 of the Ordinance which is not attracted in the present case, which was a case for depositing of rent refused by the petitioner landlord under section 19(Ka) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance. Under section 19(Ka) of the Ordinance the Court is not to see whether the tenant has paid rent within time under section 18 of the Ordinance, but whether the tenant is depositing the rent within 15 days of refusal of the rent by the landlord.
